finding.source: `path` (tag name) or `reference` argument, if attacker-influenced (e.g. tag name from CI input, PR title, or API request).

trace.note: args = (path, reference) built with no `--` separator
force=True adds kwargs['f']; with force=False no -f is added, so the caller's force guard is the only intended barrier
TagReference.create(repo, '-f', reference='v1.0') or '-d' executes git tag -f/-d v1.0
returns TagReference for 'tags/<path>', masking what happened

finding.guards_checked: Option check only blocks --file/-F (git/refs/tag.py:46, 141-146); -d and -f are not blocked. No `--` separator. No ref-name validation on path (symbolic.py _check_ref_name_valid not called here). The force parameter is bypassed by passing -f as the name.

finding.claim: Head.delete builds `git branch <flag> *heads` with no `--` separator and no validation of string head names. A name such as `-f` is parsed as a git-branch option and forces deletion of an unmerged branch even when force=False.
finding.source: `*heads` strings (type Union[Head, str]; str values are never validated). Attacker-influenced if the app builds branch names from user input.
finding.sink: repo.git.branch(flag, *heads) at git/refs/head.py:169, executed as `git branch -d -f <name>`.

trace.note: repo.git.branch('-d', '-f', 'feature') with no '--' and no name check
git's -f is the generic force flag, which skips the 'fully merged' check in -d mode

finding.guards_checked: No check_unsafe_options call in Head.delete. No `--`. No _check_ref_name_valid on str heads. The only guard is the force flag, which the injected -f bypasses. Head objects are safe (their path starts with refs/heads); the str path is the problem. Unverified: whether git accepts -f alongside -d as I expect.

finding.claim: Git.ls_remote takes a positional URL and never calls check_unsafe_protocols, unlike clone, Remote.create, set_url, fetch, push and archive. A URL such as `ext::sh -c ...` reaches git unchecked, which becomes code execution if git allows the ext transport (e.g. protocol.ext.allow=always).
finding.source: Positional `url` argument of Git().ls_remote(url), if attacker-supplied.
finding.sink: self._call_process('ls_remote', *args, **kwargs) at git/cmd.py:1144, executed as `git ls-remote <url>`.

trace.note: only option-spelled args are checked, via _option_candidates
check_unsafe_options(... unsafe_git_ls_remote_options) runs on options only
URL passes straight to git ls-remote with no check_unsafe_protocols
contrast: Remote.create calls check_unsafe_protocols(url) before running git
